text: Background: Diabetic retinopathy (DR) is a leading cause of preventable blindness, yet screening coverage in low-resource settings remains low because retinal images are scattered across hospitals that cannot share patient data. Methods: We propose a federated learning framework in which five eye hospitals jointly train a convolutional neural network for DR grading without exchanging images. Each site trains locally on fundus photographs and shares only model updates, which are aggregated with a weighted averaging scheme and protected with differential privacy noise. We evaluated the model on 48,000 images from the five sites and on an external test set of 6,500 images from a sixth site. Results: The federated model reached an area under the curve of 0.94 for referable DR, within 0.02 of a model trained on pooled data, and generalised better to the external site than any single-site model. Conclusion: Federated training can give near-pooled accuracy for DR screening while keeping images inside each hospital. Find me similar papers.
